findings.confidence: high on printed outcome; medium on novelty boundary
findings.title: Machinations has an explicit two-option Faction selection rather than the generic gain-two-Influence icon
findings.evidence: The p14 Strategy Tips inset shows the original Machinations Conflict. Its first-place reward says Choose two above the four separate gain-one-Faction icons. The extraction omits this card text. This requires one Influence in each of two different Factions, not two in one Faction.
findings.existing_coverage: Q33 tests the distinct generic gain-two-Influence icon and requires both Influence in one Faction. Q69 tests reward recipients, not resolution of the Machinations choice. Q14/Q15 test thresholds and Alliances, not selecting distinct listed reward options. Q43 chooses two Baron tokens during private setup, not how this Conflict reward distributes Influence.

source_references.section: Machinations Conflict card inset at upper right: first reward Choose two followed by Emperor, Spacing Guild, Bene Gesserit, Fremen icons
Individual gain-one-Faction icons versus generic gain-two-Influence icon

proposed_questions.question: When you win Machinations, how must its first-place Choose two reward be allocated among Factions? May you put both Influence into one Faction as with the generic gain-two-Influence icon?
proposed_questions.fixed_answer: Choose two different Factions from the four listed and gain 1 Influence with each. You cannot choose the same listed option twice. This differs from the generic gain-two-Influence icon, which gives both Influence to one chosen Faction.

source_references.section: Machinations first-place reward, visually inspected at enlarged scale
Gain named-Faction Influence; generic gain-two-Influence icon

proposed_questions.novelty: Tests an explicitly printed allocation restriction on a menu of distinct rewards. It adds the source-defined branch in which Influence must go to different Factions, whereas Q33 only tests a two-Influence effect that must stay together. It is not a changed quantity, an arithmetic example, or a recombination of two previously required effects. If the benchmark policy treats every card-specific menu as mere card data, reject on that narrower policy; the printed outcome itself is unambiguous.
